units.translation: ⟦1⟧ means a parentibus proficiscens ⟦2⟧ according to Ddf., more generally gentilis ⟦3⟧. But since certainly no listener knew of this kinship, one must now, for the sake of clarity, write with Weil ⟦4⟧ for ⟦5⟧. In the scholiast, however, another explanation is mixed in with this one, which points to the giving of gifts at the ⟦6⟧ of the child; cf. passages such as ⟦7⟧, where Xuthos sacrifices ⟦8⟧ for the seeing of his son, and especially ⟦9⟧: ⟦10⟧, ⟦11⟧, ⟦12⟧, ⟦13⟧. Certainly the scholiast read ⟦14⟧; otherwise he would not make Ph. and Leto out to be sisters. Since elsewhere (⟦15⟧ C; ⟦16⟧ ⟦17⟧; thus ⟦18⟧ = ⟦19⟧ 1127) ⟦20⟧ is the birthday festival (cf. below 293 ⟦21⟧), one can also understand ⟦22⟧ in this way, and then a closer determination of the kinship is unnecessary, even if for ⟦23⟧ Apollonios Lex. Hom. can be cited: ⟦24⟧ . . ⟦25⟧ A. ⟦26⟧, ⟦27⟧ (GHerm.). — ⟦28⟧ is usually understood as "derived name", after ⟦29⟧ ⟦30⟧; ⟦31⟧ C from the ⟦32⟧: ⟦33⟧; thus Apollo ⟦34⟧. But ⟦35⟧. also means epithet, see ⟦36⟧ ⟦37⟧, and ⟦38⟧ is in fact only an epithet (⟦39⟧ Apollonios Lex. Hom.); so I prefer to understand it thus (⟦40⟧ namely ⟦41⟧ "as epithet"). - A. has therefore, as the scholiast also notes, silently eliminated all the tales of the dragon Python, the earth-born monster which Apollo slew, and of the wrath of Gaia, and of the blood-atonement to which the god then submitted as a model. In this, however, Alkaios was already a predecessor, Frg. 2f., Preller-Robert Myth. 240, 1. Cf. also the paean of Aristonoos (Weil Mélanges de litt. et de rythm. gr. 49 ff.) 21 ff.: ⟦42⟧.
